↳ Posted by birlibirdie on June 4th, 2007.

Classical guitarist David Russell recorded this tune on his “Message of the Sea” CD, a collection of Celtic music, under the title “Loch Leven Castle”. He noted that the Loch Leven Castle is on a small island near Kinross, and was the scene of many battles between the English and the Scots from 1290 onward. He states that Mary Queen of Scots was held theree in 1567, and escaped in 1568.

Re: Loch Gamhna

Tuamgraney ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuamgraney ) is in east Clare, and if you go there
you will indeed see a (smallish) castle there, which now houses the local historical society.
If you go in, at least when we did several years ago, you will find a video of Manus Maguire playing
this tune (with lots of nice variations). I think that Manus still lives in Tuamgraey -- at least he did at one time.

Loch Leven Castle, X:7

This is how it’s often played in Scottish sessions, with a slightly dotted hornpipe feel to it.

Reminds me of happy evenings in a little rowboat fishing with my dad on Loch Leven with the castle on its island in the middle.

It’s an ancient and historic fortress that was visited by Robert the Bruce and where Mary Queen of Scots was held prisoner by the Confederate Lords.

↳ Posted by Albin Irgens on December 4th, 2022.

Taumgraney Castle, X:8

Transcribed from the playing of The Chieftains on their album 7. They called the tune “an unnamed hornpipe” and only play through the tune one full time but I love how bouncy they play this fun little hornpipe. Their version differs from most versions I’ve heard, in that they repeat the 2nd half of the A phrase both times through the B part, which to me feels like more of a classic hornpipe phrasing/composition style. This is the way that our session plays it, but typically when playing with others I play the more customary B so as not to confuse people too bad.
